title: Unraveling the spatiotemporal heterogeneity in mechanistic pathways from urban environment to mobility-associated PM2.5 exposure risk
authors: Chenyi Song; Zihao Chen; Wentao Yan
abstract: Air pollution exposure has emerged as a critical global environmental health challenge. It is essential to clarify the mechanisms linking urban environments, pollution dynamics, and human mobility. From a perspective of spatial exposure during travel, this study used mobile phone data from Shanghai to dynamically assess residents’ PM2.5 exposure throughout their workday travel trajectories. Three key indicators were introduced to characterize exposure mechanism: PM2.5 concentration (PC), travel aggregation (TA), and travel regularity (TR). By integrating machine learning and causal inference, we revealed the mechanisms and spatiotemporal heterogeneity through which urban environmental factors affect PM2.5 travel exposure risk (PTER), with particular focus on the mediating roles of PC, TA, and TR across different time periods. The results indicated the following: 1) Areas with high building and population density tended to have higher PTER, while the impacts of socioeconomic and meteorological factors are more complex. These variables display clear spatiotemporal heterogeneity and a layered, concentric spatial pattern. 2) PC, TA, and TR show distinct mediating roles. Road density and industrial land affect PTER indirectly via PC, reflecting their influence on pollution emissions. Intersection and Point of Interest densities impact PTER mainly through TR, indicating effects on travel patterns. Various density-related indicators influence PTER via TA, highlighting their role in shaping travel flow and spatial concentration. 3) The road traffic system is a key driver of PTER, with multiple mediating effects through TA, TR, and PC. Its impact varies by road hierarchy and time period. 4) Small blocks and dense road networks enhance walkability but may increase local air pollution exposure, with potential adverse health effects. This study advances the understanding of how the urban environment, air pollution, travel behavior, and exposure interact, offering valuable guidance for spatial planning and environmental policy in global megacities pursuing health-oriented air quality goals.
abstractZh: 空气污染暴露已成为全球重要的环境健康挑战，厘清城市环境、污染动态与人类移动之间的机制联系十分必要。本研究从出行过程的空间暴露视角出发，利用上海手机数据，动态评估居民工作日完整出行轨迹中的PM2.5暴露。研究引入PM2.5浓度（PC）、出行集聚（TA）和出行规律性（TR）三个关键指标，刻画暴露机制；结合机器学习与因果推断，揭示城市环境因素影响PM2.5出行暴露风险（PTER）的机制及时空异质性，重点分析PC、TA和TR在不同时段的中介作用。结果表明：（1）建筑和人口密度较高的地区通常具有较高PTER，社会经济和气象因素的影响则更加复杂；这些变量呈现明显时空异质性及分层同心圈空间格局。（2）PC、TA和TR的中介作用各不相同。道路密度和工业用地通过PC间接影响PTER，反映其对污染排放的影响；交叉口与兴趣点密度主要通过TR影响PTER，体现对出行模式的影响；多种密度指标经由TA作用于PTER，反映其塑造出行流量和空间集聚的作用。（3）道路交通系统是PTER的重要驱动因素，经由TA、TR和PC产生多重中介效应，其影响随道路等级和时段而变化。（4）小街区、密路网能够提升步行便利性，但可能增加局地空气污染暴露，带来潜在健康不利影响。本研究增进了对城市环境、空气污染、出行行为与暴露交互关系的理解，可为全球特大城市实现健康导向的空气质量目标提供空间规划和环境政策参考。
